newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Britons jailed for Cyprus killing drunk on own brew.
newsitem.headline: Britons jailed for Cyprus killing drunk on own brew.

text.p: Two Britons jailed for life for killing a Danish tour guide in Cyprus were involved in a prison fracas after getting drunk on their own brew, prison officials said on Friday.
"Some inmates squeezed grapes somebody had brought in...and got drunk on it," said George Anastassiades, director of Cyprus's central prisons.
"An inquiry is under way but they showed us how they made it and where they kept it," he told Reuters.
He confirmed that Britons Justin Fowler, 29, and Jeff Pernell, 26, were involved in the recent incident.
He dismissed reports in a Greek Cypriot newspaper suggesting that a big punch-up between convicts had occurred after the brew was distributed among foreign inmates.
"It was something instantaneous. There were no broken arms or legs," he said.

Fowler, Pernell, and Allan Ford, 29, were jailed for life by a Cyprus court last year for killing Danish tour guide Louise Jensen after a drunken binge at the holiday resort of Ayia Napa in September 1994.
The trio were with the Royal Greenjackets Regiment stationed at a British base in Cyprus at the time of the killing. They have since been discharged from the army.
Jensen, 23, from Hirtshals, Denmark, was grabbed by the three after they rammed their beach buggy into a motorcycle she was riding on with her Cypriot boyfriend.
The court found them guilty of hacking the woman to death with a spade after attempts to rape her.
They have appealed to the Supreme Court.
